Arrays, scalars, strings, null and bytes

Source: R/io-values.R
io-values.Rd

Reads and writes the Elements array, string-array, numeric-scalar, string, null and bytes (read only), all version 0.2.0 except null (0.1.0).

Usage

h5_space(dims, scalar, resizable = FALSE)

write_bool_dataset(loc, name, x, scalar, call, dataset_kwargs = list())

write_complex_dataset(loc, name, x, scalar, call, dataset_kwargs = list())

write_string_dataset(loc, name, x, scalar, call, dataset_kwargs = list())

Arguments

dims

Dimensions of the array as Python sees them.

scalar

Whether to use a scalar dataspace.

loc

An open rhdf5 file or group handle.

name

Name or path of a dataset below loc.

x

An atomic vector, matrix or array.

call

The call reported by errors.

Details

R has no scalars, so Python's rule is kept with the dim attribute:

  • a length-1 atomic vector with no dim is written as a numeric-scalar or string

  • a length-1 vector with a dim (or wrapped in as_array()) is written as a 1-element array or string-array

  • an Element read from disk remembers its Encoding type the same way, a scalar has no dim and a 1-element array has dim 1

Scalars are never compressed. Arrays have dim() equal to the shape Python sees, and a logical array without NA is written as h5py's boolean. NA_real_ and NaN are both written as NaN and read as NaN. Only complex128 is written, and reading complex64 raises anndata_dtype_error because rhdf5 reads it incorrectly. bytes is read as a raw vector. Integer, logical and character values with NA are written as the nullable Elements, see io-nullable. Complex values with NA cannot be written and raise anndata_io_registry_error.
